node.title: F2 consumer guard and depth-calibration reconciliation
node.statement: Let N=2^41, q=p^e, and B0=F_p(mu_N)=F_(p^k), with k|e and e<=6. For the depth t used by the F2 consumer, its banked generated-field guard is |B0|^t>=2^N, equivalently t*k*log2(p)>=N. Fixed-depth ambient invariance preserves the F2 census but does not preserve a depth calibration made using the ambient q. If t_C is the least integer with t_C*log2(q)>=N, then the guard holds exactly when k=e on every official degree/order type. If t*log2(q)<N, as under the exact-slice (T*) calibration, the guard fails even when k=e and hence on every official type. Therefore an exact-value mass obligation obtained by feeding (T*) into the F2 formulas is outside the banked F2 consumer scope unless that guard is explicitly overridden. The alternate non-F2 route remains open.
